 Discord release announcements no longer get cut off: they now carry a one-line digest per change and link to the full notes. [...] Run without the window: `mechvibes-dx --headless`. Starts the sounds from a terminal with no window, no tray icon and no webview, using the same keyboard capture and the same settings as the normal app. Ctrl+Alt+M still mutes, Ctrl+C exits. This also gets the app working on machines where the window itself will not open, which on Windows means a broken or missing WebView2 and on Linux a broken webkit2gtk. Add `--soundpack`  (and `--mouse-soundpack` ) to try a different pack for that run only: your saved settings are read but never written, so nothing you have set up in the app changes. results.content:
macOS: sounds only play while the app window is focused?

 Click the Mechvibes icon in the menu bar: a red "Grant Input Monitoring…" line means it is missing.
 Input Monitoring is missing or stale. See the macOS permissions notes above: remove and re-add `Mechvibes` under both Accessibility and Input Monitoring, then relaunch. A relaunch is always needed after granting Input Monitoring, even when it was simply missing.

Hotkey (`Ctrl+Alt+M`) not working?

 Windows: Run as administrator (required for global hotkey).
 Verify no other app has claimed the same hotkey.

Linux: No keyboard input detected? [...] Linux: No keyboard input detected?

 Verify user is in `input` group: `groups $USER` should list `input`.
 Re-log in for group changes to take effect.
 Check device permissions: `ls -la /dev/input/event` (should show `crw-rw---- root input`).

Soundpack won't import?

 Ensure `config.json` is valid JSON (use a JSON validator).
 Check that `definitions` (or `defs`) contains valid key mappings.
 Verify audio files (OGG, WAV, MP3, FLAC) exist and are readable.

Settings reset after restart?

 Settings are stored at: `%APPDATA%\Mechvibes` (Windows), `~/.local/share/mechvibes` (Linux), or `~/Library/Application Support/Mechvibes` (macOS). Verify these folders exist and are writable.

macOS: Right-click Open not working? [...] Linux (Fedora/RHEL):

```
sudo dnf install -y \ alsa-lib-devel \ pkg-config \ webkit2gtk4.1-devel \ gtk3-devel \ libappindicator-gtk3-devel \ librsvg2-devel \ libevdev-devel \ xdotool-devel \ libXi-devel \ libXtst-devel \ openssl-devel
```

macOS:

```
xcode-select --install
```

### Build

Development (all platforms):

```
cd
```

Run the release binary directly (macOS/Linux):

The app looks for `soundpacks/` next to the executable. `cargo build` copies the bundled packs to `target/release/soundpacks/` for you (see `build.rs`), so the binary runs as is:

```
cargo build --release ./target/release/mechvibes
```

To capture a log for a bug report, run it as `RUST_BACKTRACE=1 MECHVIBES_TRACE=1 ./target/release/mechvibes 2>&1 | tee /tmp/mv.log`.

### Look for "Open Anyway"

If the app refuses to launch at all, Gatekeeper blocked it. Open System Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll down and click "Open Anyway". This is the most upvoted fix on the Sonoma issue.

3

### On MechvibesDX, grant Input Monitoring too, then relaunch

The Rust rewrite needs both Accessibility and Input Monitoring. Without the second one it plays sounds only while its own window is focused. macOS only lets an app capture keys globally if it had the permission when it started, so a relaunch is always needed after granting it.

# Mechvibes on a Mac: what works, what breaks, and the native alternative

Mechvibes is the app most people find first when they want mechanical keyboard sounds without a mechanical keyboard. It is free, open source and runs on Windows, macOS and Linux. On a Mac, though, it is also the app behind most "no sound after the update" threads. This page explains why, how to fix it, and what changes with Haptyk, a native Mac app that reads how hard you type.

Short version: keep Mechvibes if you need free or you are on Windows or Linux. Try Haptyk if you type on an Apple Silicon MacBook and want sound that follows your hands: 3-day trial, then $8 one time.
